Another Man would confront sin without softening it.
Another Man would carry shame.
But unlike Ezra, Jesus would not merely confess alongside guilty people.
He would become the sinless Savior of guilty people.
At the cross, Christ did not pretend our sin was insignificant.
The cross proves precisely the opposite.
Our rebellion was so serious that reconciliation with God required something we could never provide for ourselves.
Christ gave Himself.
The New Testament says:
Χριστὸς ἀπέθανεν ὑπὲρ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν
Christos apethanen hyper tōn hamartiōn hēmōn.
“Christ died for our sins.”
That is the heartbeat of 1 Corinthians 15:3.
Not Christ died because humanity was basically fine.
Not Christ died so we could remain unchanged.
Christ died for our sins.
And He rose again.
That means the Gospel does something our culture cannot do.
Culture can rename you.
People can cancel you.
Shame can imprison you.
Religion without grace can crush you.
Self-help can attempt to renovate you.
But Jesus Christ can forgive you.
Cleanse you.
Reconcile you to God.
Give you a new heart.
Call you out of darkness.
And teach you to walk differently.
This is why repentance is not the enemy of grace.
Repentance runs toward grace.
The person who says, “Jesus, I have sinned. I cannot clean myself. Have mercy on me,” is not running away from the Gospel.
That person is beginning to understand it.
Maybe your clothes are not torn tonight.
Maybe there is no hair lying on the floor.
Maybe nobody knows how exhausted you are from carrying the secret.
But God knows.
He knows what happened.
He knows what you became.
He knows what you did willingly.
He knows what you regret.
He knows the promises you broke after swearing you never would.
And still the Gospel invitation stands.
Repent.
Come to Christ.
Not after you repair yourself.
Not after you become impressive.
Come bankrupt.
Come ashamed.
Come confessing.
Come believing that the blood of Jesus is sufficient for sinners.
And when Christ forgives, grace does not simply place makeup over the scandal.
Jesus begins rewriting the story.
That is what Gospel Warrior exists to keep proclaiming.
Not Christianity polished for appearances.
Not inspirational slogans without a cross.
Jesus Christ.
Scripture.
Repentance.
Grace.
Forgiveness.
Redemption.
Transformation.
More importantly, your support helps us keep building and sharing resources intended to point people toward Jesus.
Not because an algorithm deserves another post.
Because somebody you know may be smiling publicly while losing a private war.
Somebody may have convinced himself he has gone too far.
Somebody may need to discover tonight that conviction is not necessarily evidence that God has abandoned him.
It may be the mercy that finally wakes him up.
Send this to the believer who has drifted.
Share it with the person who thinks Christianity is only for people with clean histories.
And before you leave...
be honest.
Did something in this expose something you have been trying not to face?
You do not have to tell strangers your private sin.
But you can make a small declaration that you are finished pretending.
“No more hiding.”
Someone reading the comments may desperately need your testimony.
Ezra sat devastated because God's people had forgotten what their rescue was supposed to produce.
May we never become so familiar with grace that we use it as permission to return willingly to the chains from which Christ came to free us.
Because perhaps the most frightening thing about Ezra sitting there with torn clothes and hair in his hands is not how deeply he felt the horror of sin.
Perhaps it is how little we sometimes do.
Yet even there...
grace is calling.
The scandal may explain how you arrived here.
But if you surrender your story to Jesus, the scandal does not get to write the final sentence.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: GOD HEARD WHAT MIRIAM SAID WHEN MOSES DIDN’T FIGHT BACK
paragraphs:
GOD HEARD WHAT MIRIAM SAID WHEN MOSES DIDN’T FIGHT BACK
Miriam spoke against her own brother. Moses stayed quiet. Then the cloud moved—and suddenly everybody understood how seriously God had been listening.
There are sentences you forget five minutes after you say them.
And then there are sentences Heaven hears.
That is what makes Numbers 12 so uncomfortable.
Miriam was not some pagan enemy standing outside Israel throwing stones at the people of God. She was Miriam.
The woman who had already witnessed miracles.
The prophetess who took the tambourine after Israel crossed the sea.
The woman whose voice had once helped lead God's people in worship.
And yet Numbers 12 opens with something painfully ordinary.
She started talking.
“וַתְּדַבֵּר מִרְיָם וְאַהֲרֹן בְּמֹשֶׁה…”
Vattedabber Miryam ve-Aharon be-Moshe…
“Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses…”
They spoke concerning the Cushite woman Moses had married.
But almost immediately, the conversation revealed that something deeper was happening.
“Has the LORD indeed spoken only through Moses? Has He not spoken through us also?”
And then comes one of the most frightening little sentences in the chapter:
“And the LORD heard it.”
Not Moses heard it.
Not the congregation heard it.
The LORD heard it.
Sit with that.
Because suddenly this ancient wilderness story has walked straight into our homes.
Our private messages.
Our family conversations.
Our church conversations.
Our group chats.
Our whispered complaints.
Our “I’m only telling you this because I’m concerned.”
Our conversations about somebody who is not in the room to defend himself.
Sometimes we become very brave with another person's reputation when we think only trusted people are listening.
But God was listening when Miriam spoke.
And God is still listening.

This passage does not teach that every criticism of spiritual leadership is sinful. Scripture itself commands discernment, accountability, truth, and confrontation of genuine sin. Biblical leaders are never granted immunity from correction merely because they lead.
Numbers 12 is dealing with something more specific.
Miriam and Aaron were challenging Moses, and beneath their words was a question of spiritual status:
Why Moses?
Hasn't God spoken through us too?
And God Himself answered.
Moses did not have to launch a campaign defending his reputation.
He did not gather supporters.
He did not release a statement.
He did not destroy Miriam publicly.
God called all three of them to the tent of meeting.
Then the LORD descended in the pillar of cloud.
Imagine the silence.
Miriam had spoken about Moses.
Now God was going to speak about Moses.
God explained that although He revealed Himself to prophets through visions and dreams, Moses occupied a unique position in the covenant administration of Israel.
“My servant Moses is not so, who is faithful in all mine house.”
God spoke with him with extraordinary directness.
Then came the question Miriam could not answer:
Why were you not afraid to speak against My servant Moses?
The issue was no longer merely Miriam versus Moses.
Her words had collided with God.
And Scripture says:
“The anger of the LORD was kindled against them.”
Then the cloud departed.
And when it did, Aaron looked toward Miriam.
Something had happened.
The Hebrew says:
וְהִנֵּה מִרְיָם מְצֹרַעַת כַּשָּׁלֶג
Vehinneh Miryam metzora'at kashaleg.
“Behold, Miriam was afflicted with a severe skin disease, like snow.”

Older English translations commonly use “leprous,” while modern translations often use language such as “defiling skin disease.” The Hebrew terminology associated with tzara'at covers conditions that should not simply be identified with what modern medicine calls Hansen's disease.
But whatever the precise medical nature of Miriam's condition, the theological point of Numbers 12 is unmistakable.
God had judged her.
The woman who had spoken became the woman standing exposed.
And suddenly Aaron's vocabulary changed.
No more comparison.
No more “Hasn't God spoken through us?”
Now there was confession.
“We have done foolishly.”
“We have sinned.”
Amazing how quickly pride loses its vocabulary when holiness enters the room.
And perhaps that is where this story stops being about Miriam.
Because some of us know exactly what it feels like to discover that something we justified was actually sin.
You called it frustration.
God called you toward repentance.
You called it venting.
But somewhere along the way, another person's dignity became entertainment.
You called it discernment.
But secretly you enjoyed exposing them.
You called it honesty.
But love had disappeared from your honesty a long time ago.
You said, “I'm just saying what happened.”
But deep inside, you knew why you were saying it.
That is the terrifying thing about sin.
We can rename it until it sounds respectable.
God still sees the heart.
Yet Numbers 12 contains something even more astonishing than Miriam's judgment.
Watch Moses.
This is the man they spoke against.
This is the brother they challenged.
This is the person who had every human reason to say:
“Now you understand.”
Instead, Moses prayed.
The Hebrew is breathtakingly short:
אֵל נָא רְפָא נָא לָהּ
El na, refa na lah.
“O God, please heal her.”
That's it.
No speech about how badly she hurt him.
No demand that she apologize publicly first.
No celebration of her downfall.
The wounded man interceded for the woman who wounded him.
And suddenly Numbers 12 begins whispering forward toward Someone greater than Moses.
Jesus.
Because Moses can point us toward mercy, but Moses cannot become our final Savior.
Jesus can.
Centuries later, another rejected Servant would stand beneath accusations.
He would be mocked.
Betrayed.
Falsely accused.
Struck.
Humiliated.
Crucified.
And from the cross would come words of mercy:
“Father, forgive them.”
This is where the Gospel destroys both our pride and our despair.
Because some readers see themselves in Moses.
Someone spoke about you.
Someone twisted your intentions.
Someone damaged your reputation.
Someone you loved became the person carrying the knife.
And everything inside you wants vindication.
Numbers 12 asks a devastating question:
Can you pray for the person who wounded you?
Not pretend the wound never happened.
Not call evil good.
Not refuse appropriate boundaries or accountability.
But can you bring that person before God without secretly hoping God destroys them?
Moses could.
And Jesus went infinitely further.
But perhaps you do not see yourself in Moses.
Perhaps you see yourself in Miriam.
That is harder.
Maybe you were the one who talked.
Maybe jealousy found a religious vocabulary.
Maybe bitterness became gossip.
Maybe you damaged someone and only realized the weight of it afterward.
Maybe your mouth exposed something ugly inside your heart.
Then hear this carefully:
Miriam's story did not end outside the camp.
God required seven days of exclusion.
Consequences remained.
Grace did not pretend nothing happened.
But after seven days…
she was brought back.
Do not miss those words.
Brought.
Back.
The same chapter containing judgment also contains restoration.
The same Miriam who experienced disgrace was not permanently abandoned.
And the entire congregation waited until she returned.
That is biblical grace.
Grace is not God pretending sin does not matter.
The cross forever destroys that shallow definition.
Sin matters so profoundly that the Son of God bore judgment for sinners.
Grace means sinners who deserve judgment can be forgiven, cleansed, reconciled, and brought home because Jesus Christ paid what they could never pay.
Maybe you have spent years believing the worst thing you ever did deserves to become your permanent name.
Adulterer.
Liar.
Gossip.
Addict.
Hypocrite.
Failure.
Backslider.
Dirty.
Unworthy.
Finished.
But Scripture tells a different story about everyone who truly comes to Christ.
Repentance does not mean pretending the scandal never happened.
It means bringing the scandal into the light and surrendering it to the Savior whose blood is greater than your guilt.
Jesus does not rewrite everything by rewriting history.
He rewrites everything by redeeming people history seemed to have finished.
That is why the Gospel is so offensive to pride and so beautiful to the broken.
You cannot save yourself.
You cannot talk yourself clean.
You cannot perform enough religious activity to erase your guilt.
You need mercy.
You need forgiveness.
You need Christ.
And perhaps the sentence you most need to hear today is not “God heard Miriam.”
Perhaps it is this:
God brought Miriam back.
The God who disciplines is also the God who restores.
The God who exposes sin also calls sinners to repentance.
And in Jesus Christ, condemnation does not get the final word over those who belong to Him.
“There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus.”
Maybe God used this story to expose something in you.
Talk to Him.
If you have been destroying people with your words, repent.
If jealousy has been hiding beneath spiritual language, repent.
If bitterness has turned another person's failure into your entertainment, repent.
If someone wounded you and hatred has slowly occupied your heart, bring that wound to Jesus.
And if shame has convinced you that you have been outside the camp too long to ever come home…
look at the cross.
Christ receives repentant sinners.
There is forgiveness in Him.
There is cleansing in Him.
There is a new beginning in Him.
There is no scandal so powerful that the grace of Jesus becomes powerless.
And if somebody came into your mind while reading this, don't use this article as a weapon against them.
Pray for them.
Then, if sharing it would genuinely help them, send it with love.
Supporting Gospel-centered teaching is not what glorifies God by itself—Christ is glorified through faithful obedience, generosity, truth, love, and lives transformed by His Gospel.
Because Christianity is not the announcement that good people finally became good enough.
It is the announcement that sinners can be reconciled to a holy God through Jesus Christ.
But before you leave, remember the scene.
Miriam outside the camp.
Seven days.
A nation waiting.
A woman carrying the consequences of words she could never pull back into her mouth.
And then…
she came back.
Perhaps that is why you found this today.
Not so you could stare at Miriam's punishment.
But so you could finally understand what grace does after sin has been exposed.
Your worst chapter may explain why you need the cross—but it does not get to write the ending when Jesus holds the pen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: 🚨 YOU CAN PREACH FROM THE BIBLE EVERY WEEK… AND STILL FAIL TO PREACH CHRIST.
paragraphs: 🚨 YOU CAN PREACH FROM THE BIBLE EVERY WEEK… AND STILL FAIL TO PREACH CHRIST.
That sentence may sting.
But every preacher, teacher, ministry leader, and serious student of Scripture needs to wrestle with it.
You can preach David and tell people to defeat their giants.
You can preach Joseph and tell people to pursue their dreams.
You can preach Nehemiah and give leadership principles.
You can preach Proverbs and offer life advice.
All of those sermons may contain biblical truth…
But where is CHRIST?
Where is the GOSPEL?
Where is the call to repentance, faith, grace, and obedience?
And there is another danger:
Trying so hard to find Jesus in every passage that we begin forcing meanings into Scripture that aren't actually there.
There has to be a better way.
📖 HOW TO PREACH CHRIST FROM ANY BIBLICAL TEXT
A Practical Guide to Christ-Centered, Gospel-Faithful Preaching Without Forcing Jesus Into the Passage
Jesus told His disciples that the Scriptures testify about Him.
And after His resurrection:
📖 “Beginning with Moses and all the Prophets, he interpreted to them in all the Scriptures the things concerning himself.” — Luke 24:27
This book will help you understand what that means for the way you study, teach, and preach God's Word.
Not by inventing secret meanings.
Not by turning every object into an allegory.
Not by ignoring historical context.
And not by simply adding Jesus to the last five minutes of your sermon.
Instead, you'll learn a practical framework:
⚔️ TEXT → CONTEXT → REDEMPTIVE STORY → CHRIST → GOSPEL → RESPONSE
📖 INSIDE YOU'LL DISCOVER:
• How to determine what a biblical passage actually means before preaching it
• How to see individual passages within the Bible's unfolding story of redemption
• How to preach Christ from Old Testament narratives without turning them into forced allegories
• How to approach the Law, Psalms, Proverbs, Prophets, and difficult passages
• How to recognize legitimate promises, patterns, themes, and biblical connections that lead toward Christ
• How to avoid shallow moralistic preaching that reduces Christianity to “try harder and behave better”
• How to move naturally from the biblical text to Christ and the Gospel
• How to call people toward repentance, faith, worship, obedience, and hope
• How to prepare sermons that are faithful to Scripture rather than merely impressive to listeners
🔥 HERE'S THE DIVIDE.
Most people want a sermon that sounds powerful.
Few will labor to make sure it is faithful.
Most want people to remember the preacher.
Few are satisfied when people leave remembering Christ.
Most ask:
“How can I make this passage relevant?”
Few first ask:
“What has God actually said?”
Most want another preaching technique.
Few want their entire approach to Scripture transformed.
If God has entrusted you with an opportunity to teach His Word, you are handling something far greater than content.
You are handling the Word of God.
And that deserves humility.
Study.
Prayer.
Faithfulness.
And a determination to proclaim Christ without manipulating Scripture.
It's part of a growing discipleship movement built around one mission:

⚔️ PROCLAIM CHRIST.
📖 TEACH THE WORD.
🔥 MAKE DISCIPLES.
🌍 SPREAD THE GOSPEL.
Including:

📚 Books
👕 T-shirts
☕ Mugs
📓 Journals
🎁 And more Gospel Warrior resources
Your support helps us keep writing.
Keep teaching.
Keep creating.
And keep putting Gospel-centered resources into people's hands.
⚔️ THIS ISN'T JUST ABOUT GETTING ANOTHER BOOK.
It's about becoming the kind of believer who says:
“If God gives me His Word to teach, I want to handle it faithfully.”
If you're a pastor…
Preacher…
Bible teacher…
Small-group leader…
Ministry worker…
Or simply a believer hungry to understand Scripture more deeply…
This is for you.
Then don't keep the message to yourself.
⚔️ WE DON'T NEED MORE SERMONS THAT MAKE MUCH OF THE PREACHER.

title: A church can survive disagreement. It may not survive unchecked division.
paragraphs:
A church can survive disagreement.
It may not survive unchecked division.
And here’s the uncomfortable part:
Sometimes the person spreading division is convinced they’re defending the truth.

📖 HOW TO DEAL WITH A DIVISIVE CHURCH MEMBER BIBLICALLY
Confronting Division With Truth, Grace, and Godly Wisdom
Church division rarely begins with someone announcing:
“I’m going to divide this church.”
It starts quietly.
A private offense.
A whispered complaint.
A conversation that should have stayed between two people.
Then someone takes a side.
Someone else repeats the story.
Suspicion grows.
Relationships fracture.
And suddenly people who once worshiped together can barely look at each other.
But there’s another danger:
Not everyone who disagrees with you is divisive.
Sometimes legitimate correction gets labeled “rebellion.”
Sometimes gossip gets disguised as “discernment.”
Sometimes bitterness gets called “standing for truth.”
And sometimes people demand “unity” when what they really want is silence.
🔥 THAT’S WHY I WROTE THIS BOOK.
This isn't a guide for winning church arguments.
It's about learning how to respond biblically when conflict threatens the Body of Christ.
Inside, you’ll discover:

• How to recognize the difference between disagreement and genuine division
• Why Scripture takes gossip and faction-building seriously
• How Matthew 18 teaches us to confront problems directly
• What to do when private correction doesn't work
• How to pursue reconciliation without compromising truth
• When biblical boundaries may become necessary
• Why “church unity” must never become an excuse for hiding sin
• How to examine whether you might be contributing to the conflict
• How to become a peacemaker without becoming passive
• How truth, repentance, grace, and forgiveness can bring healing
⚔️ MOST PEOPLE VS. THE GOSPEL WARRIOR
Most people hear gossip and become an audience.
Few say: “Have you spoken to that person directly?”
Most people want everyone to know when they’ve been wronged.
Few want reconciliation more than vindication.
Most people examine the other person.
Few ask God to examine them first.
Most people choose a side.
Mature believers choose truth, grace, and obedience to Christ.
Jesus said:
“Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.” — Matthew 5:9 KJV
The question isn't merely:
“Who is right?”
Sometimes the deeper question is:
“Am I responding in a way that honors Christ?”
It is to proclaim the Gospel, call people to repentance, strengthen believers, encourage obedience to Christ, and help spread the Word of God to more people.
But the greatest reason to join isn't the discount.
It's the mission.
If you want to honor God by helping support the spread of His Word, and you want access to resources that challenge you to grow in truth, repentance, faith, and obedience—
⚔️ JOIN THE GOSPEL WARRIOR MOVEMENT.
Don't just be someone who complains about what is wrong with the Church.
Become someone who helps strengthen it.

Truth without love can wound.
Love without truth can compromise.
But biblical truth spoken in love can lead toward restoration.

⚔️ GOSPEL WARRIOR
Truth. Repentance. Grace. Obedience. Jesus Christ.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: 🚨 YOU CAN BUILD A CHURCH… AND STILL LOSE YOUR CHILDREN.
paragraphs: 🚨 YOU CAN BUILD A CHURCH… AND STILL LOSE YOUR CHILDREN.
Read that again, pastor.

You can preach powerful sermons.
Counsel broken marriages.
Answer midnight calls.
Lead ministries.
Disciple hundreds.
And still come home to children who barely know you.
That should confront us.
Because ministry success is never permission for family neglect.

HOW TO PASTOR WITHOUT NEGLECTING YOUR CHILDREN
Building a Faithful Ministry Without Sacrificing the Family God Entrusted to You
Pastors are constantly told to sacrifice for the ministry.

More meetings.
More counseling.
More availability.
More programs.
More people needing you.
But there is a dangerous question every ministry leader eventually needs to answer:
Are you shepherding everyone else's family while slowly becoming absent from your own?
Your congregation needs a pastor.
Your children need their father.
This book was created for pastors, ministry leaders, church planters, and future pastors who refuse to believe that destroying their family is the price they must pay for obeying God.
🔥 INSIDE THIS BOOK, YOU'LL DISCOVER:

• How to recognize when ministry has begun competing with your family
• Biblical principles for leading your household while shepherding God's people
• How to create boundaries without abandoning people who genuinely need pastoral care
• Why your children need your presence—not merely your reputation
• How to disciple your children without making them perform Christianity for the church
• How to protect pastors' kids from unhealthy expectations and ministry pressure
• Practical rhythms for family time, rest, ministry emergencies, and one-on-one connection
• What to do when you realize you have already neglected your family
• How repentance, listening, forgiveness, and consistency can begin rebuilding damaged relationships
• How to pursue a ministry your family can serve alongside without being crushed by it
Scripture says:
“But as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD.” — Joshua 24:15
⚔️ MOST PEOPLE VS. THE FAITHFUL FEW
Most people measure ministry by attendance.
Few ask what is happening at home.
Most celebrate the pastor everyone can reach.
Few consider whether his own children can reach him.
Most want a bigger ministry.
Few are willing to establish the boundaries required for a healthier family.
Most want to leave a ministry legacy.
Few realize their children are part of that legacy.
Pastor, the goal isn't simply to finish ministry with people applauding you.
The goal is faithfulness to Christ in the pulpit AND in the home.
And there's another benefit.
⚔️ THIS IS BIGGER THAN ONE BOOK.
We want to raise believers who take God's Word seriously.
Pastors who shepherd without sacrificing their homes.
Fathers who understand that presence is ministry too.
Families that love Jesus without resenting the church.
Leaders who would rather be faithful than famous.
If that is the kind of Christian leader you want to become, join us.
Then do three things:

Build the ministry.
Shepherd the people.
Preach the Word.
Love your family.
⚔️ GOSPEL WARRIOR
Faithful families. Stronger churches. Brighter generations.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: 🚨 YOUR FIRST SERMON DOESN’T NEED TO SOUND POWERFUL. IT NEEDS TO BE FAITHFUL.
paragraphs: 🚨 YOUR FIRST SERMON DOESN’T NEED TO SOUND POWERFUL. IT NEEDS TO BE FAITHFUL.
You feel called to preach.
Then you open your Bible to prepare…
And suddenly the questions hit.

Where do I start?
What passage should I choose?
How do I build an outline?
What if I interpret something incorrectly?
What if I freeze when I stand in front of people?
Here’s the mistake many first-time preachers make:
They focus so much on how they will sound that they forget the greater responsibility—
What does God’s Word actually say?

🔥 HOW TO PREPARE YOUR FIRST SERMON STEP BY STEP
A Biblical Guide for First-Time Preachers
“Preach the word.” — 2 Timothy 4:2
This isn't a book about becoming a celebrity preacher.
It’s about becoming a faithful messenger of Jesus Christ.

Whether you're preparing your first church sermon, devotional, Bible study, youth message, or ministry teaching, this guide walks you through the process—from the moment you open your Bible to the moment you stand up and preach.
🔥 INSIDE, YOU’LL LEARN:

• How to begin sermon preparation with prayer
• How to choose a focused biblical passage
• How to study Scripture in context
• How to discover the main message of the text
• How to build a clear, simple sermon outline
• How to write an introduction that captures attention
• How to explain Scripture before applying it
• How to create practical, biblical application
• How to keep Jesus Christ at the center
• How to prepare a strong conclusion
• How to practice your sermon effectively
• How to handle nervousness before preaching
• How to evaluate yourself and improve after preaching
⚔️ HERE'S THE DIFFERENCE:

Most people want to sound anointed.
Few are willing to study deeply.

Most want the microphone.
Few embrace preparation.

Most want people to remember the preacher.
Faithful servants want people to remember Jesus.
Most ask:
“How can I impress them?”
The Gospel Warrior asks:
“How can I faithfully proclaim God's Word?”
That difference can shape an entire ministry.
It helps support the continued creation and sharing of Christ-centered resources designed to spread the Word of God.
⚔️ THIS IS BIGGER THAN ONE BOOK.
We're building a movement of believers who want more than inspirational Christianity.
Believers who study the Word.
Believers who pray.
Believers who repent.
Believers who obey.
Believers who disciple others.
Believers who aren't ashamed of Jesus Christ.
And believers willing to say:
“Lord, if You give me an opportunity to speak, help me handle Your Word faithfully.”
🔥 READY TO PREPARE YOUR FIRST SERMON?
Don't chase the platform.
Don't chase applause.
Don't try to become somebody else.

Open the Bible.
Study faithfully.
Pray deeply.
Love the people.
Point them to Jesus.
PREACH THE WORD.

GOSPEL WARRIOR
Equipping believers. Strengthening disciples. Proclaiming Jesus Christ.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: 🚨 YOUR MINISTRY TITLE WILL NOT MAKE YOU IMMUNE TO SEXUAL TEMPTATION.
paragraphs: 🚨 YOUR MINISTRY TITLE WILL NOT MAKE YOU IMMUNE TO SEXUAL TEMPTATION.
You can preach on Sunday…
and secretly fight temptation on Monday.
You can lead worship, counsel people, pray for others, know Scripture—and still have areas of your heart that desperately need guarding.
The dangerous thought is:
“That could never happen to me.”
Because many devastating ministry failures didn’t begin with an affair.
They began with a message.
A private conversation.
A second look.
Pornography nobody knew about.
An emotional connection that felt “innocent.”
A boundary moved little by little.
Until something once unthinkable became possible.
HOW TO PROTECT YOURSELF FROM SEXUAL TEMPTATION IN MINISTRY
Guarding Your Heart, Your Calling, Your Marriage, and the People God Entrusted to You
This isn't written to shame struggling Christians.
It's written to help you fight before temptation becomes destruction.
Scripture says:
“Therefore let anyone who thinks that he stands take heed lest he fall.” — 1 Corinthians 10:12
And Paul tells Timothy:
“Flee youthful passions and pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace.” — 2 Timothy 2:22
🔥 INSIDE THIS BOOK, YOU'LL LEARN:

• How sexual compromise often begins long before anything physical happens
• How to recognize emotional affairs before they become sexual
• Why secrecy makes temptation far more dangerous
• Practical boundaries for counseling, messaging, travel, and ministry relationships
• How pornography can undermine private integrity
• Why Joseph's response in Genesis 39 gives us a powerful model: FLEE
• How to recognize your most vulnerable seasons
• How to build accountability that actually works
• How to protect your marriage while serving others
• What genuine repentance looks like when boundaries have already been crossed
• How to create your own Ministry Purity Protection Plan
⚔️ MOST PEOPLE WAIT UNTIL TEMPTATION BECOMES A CRISIS.
Few build boundaries beforehand.
Most believe they can handle one more conversation.
Few recognize when emotional intimacy is already developing.
Most want to protect their reputation after something happens.
Few are willing to protect their character before anyone is watching.
Don't ask:
“How close can I get without technically sinning?”
Ask:
“What must I protect so I can remain faithful to Jesus?”
Your calling is worth guarding.
Your marriage is worth guarding.
Your mind is worth guarding.
And the people God entrusted to your ministry are worth protecting.
⚔️ THIS IS THE GOSPEL WARRIOR MOVEMENT.
Not perfect Christians pretending they never struggle.
Believers choosing light over secrecy.
Repentance over excuses.
Boundaries over compromise.
Obedience over temporary pleasure.
Jesus over everything.
Then don't keep this message to yourself.
Someone fighting privately may need this message today.
“Flee youthful passions and pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace.” — 2 Timothy 2:22

GUARD YOUR HEART.
PROTECT YOUR CALLING.
STAY FAITHFUL.
— GOSPEL WARRIOR
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: 🚨 YOUR CHURCH CAN BE FULL… AND STILL FAIL TO MAKE DISCIPLES.
paragraphs: 🚨 YOUR CHURCH CAN BE FULL… AND STILL FAIL TO MAKE DISCIPLES.
That should concern every Christian leader.
Jesus never said, “Go and build an audience.”
He said:
“Go therefore and make disciples of all nations…” — Matthew 28:19
But here’s the problem:
Many believers know how to invite people to church.
Few know how to take someone from new believer → grounded disciple → mature servant → disciple-maker.
And when there is no clear pathway, people can attend for years while remaining spiritually dependent.
That is exactly why I created:

📖 HOW TO BUILD A DISCIPLESHIP SYSTEM FROM ZERO
A Biblical Blueprint for Turning New Believers Into Mature, Multiplying Followers of Jesus
You don’t need a massive ministry.
You don’t need expensive software.
You don’t need a complicated curriculum.
You need a biblical process that ordinary believers can actually reproduce.
This book will show you how to build one.
📖 WHAT YOU’LL LEARN
Inside, you’ll discover:

• How to define what a biblical disciple actually looks like
• How to build a clear pathway from conversion to spiritual maturity
• How to establish new believers in Scripture, prayer, repentance, fellowship, and obedience
• How to create healthy accountability without controlling people
• How to move Christians from consumers to servants
• How to train believers to become disciple-makers
• How to measure transformation instead of attendance
• How to build a simple system that can multiply from one person to another
• How to begin even when you have no staff, no budget, and no existing program
Because discipleship was never supposed to end with you.
Paul told Timothy:
“…entrust to faithful men, who will be able to teach others also.” — 2 Timothy 2:2
That is the multiplication pattern:
PAUL → TIMOTHY → FAITHFUL PEOPLE → OTHERS
It is a call to recover the mission Jesus gave His Church.

Most people want followers.
Few are willing to make disciples.

Most people measure attendance.
Few measure transformation.

Most people want a platform.
Few will patiently invest in one person.
Most people ask:
“How many people are following me?”
Disciple-makers ask:
“Who am I helping follow Jesus?”
Which one are you becoming?
⚔️ DON’T JUST CONSUME CHRISTIAN CONTENT. BECOME A DISCIPLE WHO MAKES DISCIPLES.
If that is the kind of believer you want to become:
This isn't merely about building another ministry program.
It's about multiplying faithful followers of Jesus.

ONE DISCIPLE.
MAKING ANOTHER DISCIPLE.
WHO MAKES ANOTHER.
That is how multiplication begins.

GOSPEL WARRIOR ⚔️
Books. Bold Truth. Real Transformation.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: 🚨 IF YOUR CHURCH CAN’T FUNCTION WITHOUT YOU, YOU HAVEN’T FINISHED BUILDING IT.
paragraphs: 🚨 IF YOUR CHURCH CAN’T FUNCTION WITHOUT YOU, YOU HAVEN’T FINISHED BUILDING IT.
That may be uncomfortable.
But every pastor, church planter, and ministry leader needs to wrestle with this question:
What would happen to the ministry if you disappeared for 90 days?
Would disciples keep being made?
Would leaders keep leading?
Would people still be cared for?
Would decisions still be made?
Would the mission continue?
Or would everything start falling apart because you became the system?

HOW TO BUILD A CHURCH THAT CAN FUNCTION WITHOUT YOU
From Pastor-Dependent Ministry to a Christ-Centered Culture of Disciples, Leaders, and Multiplication
Jesus never intended one leader to carry the entire church.
He developed disciples.
He entrusted responsibility.
He sent people into ministry.
He prepared them to lead.
And before ascending, He commissioned them to make more disciples.
Paul taught the same principle:
“And what you have heard from me... entrust to faithful men, who will be able to teach others also.” — 2 Timothy 2:2
That is multiplication.
Paul → Timothy → faithful people → others.
And perhaps most importantly:
You’ll learn the difference between building a ministry around your gift and building people around Christ.
⚔️ MOST PEOPLE VS. FEW PEOPLE
Most leaders want more followers.
Few intentionally raise replacements.
Most want a bigger congregation.
Few build stronger disciples.
Most celebrate how much the pastor can do.
Few ask how much the pastor has equipped others to do.
Most build for Sunday.
Few build for the next generation.
Your greatest legacy will not be that people couldn't function without you.
It will be that because you faithfully equipped them, they learned to follow Christ, serve others, raise leaders, and make disciples.
We are building a movement of believers who refuse to remain spectators.
Disciples who make disciples.
Leaders who raise leaders.
Servants who equip servants.
Churches centered on Christ rather than personalities.
And believers determined to carry the Gospel forward.

Build disciples.
Raise leaders.
Release ministry.
Multiply the mission.
Christ must remain the Head of His Church.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)
